summary: Ton Lam Yai is the riverside market beside Warorot (Kad Luang), best known for its flower trade. The covered market also has everyday grocery and household stalls; its all-hours reputation applies chiefly to flower trading, not necessarily every indoor shop.
whyGo: See a working flower market along the Ping River, with garlands and fresh flowers traded beyond ordinary retail hours.
Pair it with adjacent Warorot Market for northern Thai snacks and shopping, then walk the nearby riverfront and bridges.
bestFor: Travelers curious about local flower commerce, market photography and everyday Chiang Mai trade.
A flexible add-on to Warorot Market, with an evening option for the flower stalls.
skipIf: You expect a curated attraction, formal visitor facilities or a reliably quiet route.
You need confirmed step-free access throughout; accessibility details are not published.
duration: Allow 30–60 minutes for a browse; plan 1–2 hours if combining it with Warorot and the riverside. These are itinerary estimates.
cost: No admission fee is indicated. Purchases are optional; flower and food prices depend on the seller and item, so ask before buying.
hours: The flower market is described by travel references as operating around the clock, with much of the flower trade after dark and before dawn. Covered-market grocery and household stalls keep their own hours and may close earlier; no authoritative stall-by-stall schedule was found.
bestTime: For the flower market, visit after dark or before dawn for the most active trade; daytime works for a relaxed look at the wider market district. The exact peak varies by day and season.
gettingThere: At 88/1 Wichayanon Road in Chang Moi, on the Ping River beside Warorot Market. Ask for Ton Lam Yai or Kad Luang; walk from central Chiang Mai or use a songthaew, tuk-tuk or ride-hail. Travel time varies with traffic.
booking: No ticket or advance booking is indicated; browse independently. Carry small cash for purchases and confirm the price before ordering.
accessibility: No formal accessibility information was found. Expect a working market with potentially busy, narrow or wet passages; stairs or step-free routes within the covered areas are unconfirmed. Contact a local operator or check in person if step-free access is essential.
practicalTips: Treat the 24-hour claim as applying to the flower-trading area; do not assume every covered shop or food stall is open all night.
Pair with Warorot Market across the street, but check its separate daytime hours if you want to shop there.
Wear shoes with good grip around wet flower work areas, keep valuables secure, and ask before photographing people or stalls.
Use the river as an orientation point; the market is near Chansom Memorial Bridge and the central market district.
decemberNotes: December is a practical cool-season time to visit Chiang Mai, but no specific Ton Lam Yai event or 2026 holiday schedule was confirmed. The flower market is described as active year-round; verify local conditions if timing a late-night or dawn visit. December 2026 stall hours and any temporary closures remain unconfirmed.
uncertainties: The all-hours description comes from visitor guides and refers chiefly to flower trading; no official current schedule by market section or stall was found.
No formal accessibility statement, current price list, or December 2026 event/holiday schedule was located.
